transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… the main thing is that I keep making myself throw up after I eat. It’s hard to say out loud, honestly. Sometimes I do it in the bathroom at work, like if I’ve eaten and then I start feeling panicky or just wrong in my body, and sometimes I wait until I get home and go straight to the bathroom.

It’s gotten to where it feels like the only thing that calms me down, even though I hate it. I hate that I do it, and I hate that part of me feels relieved afterward. That’s why I’m here, because it’s starting to scare me how much I feel like I need to do it.
Do you think about your weight when you feel the need to throw up after eating?

Yes… definitely. It’s almost always about that, even if I don’t admit it to myself right away.

Like, if I step on the scale and it’s up even a little bit — even a tiny amount — my whole mood just drops. I start panicking like I’ve ruined everything, like whatever I ate has already changed my body. Or if I’m at work and my waistband feels tight under my apron, I can’t stop thinking about it. I keep noticing it every time I bend or move, and it’s like this alarm going off in my head that I’m going to be fat by the end of the day if I don’t do something.

I know that probably sounds dramatic, but in the moment it feels so real. Like I can’t just sit with it. That fear gets so loud that throwing up feels like the only way to make it quiet down.
Do you often limit the amount or type of food you eat to try to control your weight?

Yeah… I do. I mean, I’ll tell myself I’m just “being careful” or “getting back on track,” but really it’s because I’m scared of gaining weight.

Like if I feel like I ate too much the day before, the next day I’ll try not to eat until really late. I’ll drink coffee or water and keep telling myself I can wait a little longer, even if I’m shaky or my stomach is making noise. At work it’s a little easier to pretend I’m just busy, because I’m on my feet at the cleaners all day and there’s always something to fold or tag or press, but in my head I’m counting the hours and thinking about what I’m allowed to have later.

And sometimes I try to make up for eating by walking a lot or exercising, even when I’m already exhausted. My legs will hurt from standing all day, like actually ache, but I’ll still make myself keep moving because I feel like I have to undo what I ate. It’s not really about feeling healthy. It feels more like punishment, I guess. Like I don’t deserve to just eat normally if I messed up.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

I… I don’t really know how to answer that. I mean, I check my weight a lot, so I notice every little change, but I don’t know if it would count as “significant” the way you mean it.

There are times it goes down and I feel almost… relieved, like I did something right, and then if it goes up even a little I get really upset. But I can’t say I’ve had some big obvious weight loss that other people are commenting on or anything. At least, not that I can tell. I think I’m more just constantly watching it and reacting to every small number, if that makes sense.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, like within an hour or two, and feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?

Yes… yes, that happens. I hate saying that out loud, but it does.

It’s like once I start eating, something just… switches off, or maybe switches on, I don’t know. I can be telling myself the whole time, “Stop, just stop now, put it away,” and then my hands are still reaching for more food anyway. It feels almost like I’m watching myself do it from the outside, like I know what I’m doing and I know I’m going to feel awful about it, but I can’t make myself quit in that moment.

And it’s not like I’m enjoying it the way you’re supposed to enjoy food. At first maybe there’s this relief, like I finally get to eat, but then very quickly it turns into this panicky thing where I’m just grabbing and chewing and thinking, “Why am I still doing this?” But I keep going. Even if I feel full, even if I’m embarrassed, even if I’m promising myself every few seconds that this is the last bite. It doesn’t feel controlled. It feels like my body is moving faster than my brain can stop it.
Is making yourself throw up mostly about trying to control your weight?

Yeah… mostly, yes. I mean, I tell myself different things in the moment, like I’m just trying to feel less full or make the panic stop, but underneath it, it’s about weight. It’s about feeling like I ruined everything by eating and I have to get it out of me before it “counts,” if that makes sense.

That’s actually a big part of why I’m here. I keep making myself throw up after I eat, and it’s gotten to where it doesn’t even feel like a choice sometimes. I’ll eat and then my mind goes straight to, “You have to fix this.” Sometimes I do it in the bathroom at work, which makes me feel so ashamed because I’m trying to be quiet and normal and then go back out like nothing happened. Or I’ll hold it together until I get home and then go straight to the bathroom.

And I hate saying this, but it’s started to feel like the only way I can calm down after eating. Like I know it’s not okay, I know it’s disgusting and scary, but in that moment the fear is so loud that throwing up feels like the only thing that quiets it for a little while.
How often do you have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short period of time?

For months now, it’s been happening most weeks… not every single day, but usually at least a couple times in a week. Sometimes more, depending on how things are going.

It’s usually like I eat way more than I meant to in a short amount of time, and then afterward I get this awful panic, like I have to undo it somehow. A lot of the time that means making myself throw up, but sometimes I’ll try not eating for a while after, or I’ll exercise because I feel like I have to burn it off. It’s not just once in a while anymore. It’s been this pattern for months, and I keep telling myself it was the last time, but then the next week it happens again.
How often do you make yourself throw up after eating?

It’s… it’s often. More often than I want to admit.

A lot of the time after I eat, especially if I feel like I ate too much, my mind goes straight to needing to throw up. Sometimes I’ll do it right away, like if I’m at work I’ll go into the bathroom and try to be quiet and act normal afterward, which makes me feel horrible. Other times I’ll hold it in until I get home, and then it’s like the first thing I do is go to the bathroom because I can’t calm down until I’ve done it.

It’s not every single time I eat, but it’s become… I don’t know, this regular thing. Like after eating, if that panic starts, throwing up feels like the only way I can make it stop. And I hate that. I hate that it feels like the thing I rely on now, because I know it’s not normal and I feel so ashamed afterward, but in the moment I feel desperate.
Have you noticed your clothes fitting differently due to weight loss?

I’m not really sure. I mean… I pay attention to my body a lot, probably too much, but with my clothes it’s hard for me to say if they’re actually fitting differently or if I’m just feeling different in them.

Some days I put something on and I’m convinced it feels looser or tighter, but then I don’t know if that’s real or if I’m just checking and overthinking it. I haven’t had, like, a clear moment where all my clothes are suddenly falling off me or anything like that. I just… I don’t trust my own sense of it very much.
Do you make yourself throw up after every episode of eating a large amount of food in a short period of time?

Not every single time, no… but a lot of the time, yes. Enough that it feels like that’s the pattern now.

If I have one of those episodes where I eat a lot and I feel like I went too far, it’s like my head immediately starts screaming at me that I have to get it out. Sometimes I try to sit with it for a little while, or I tell myself I’m not going to do it this time, but then I get so worked up and panicky that I end up going to the bathroom anyway.

And it’s not just at home, which is part of what scares me. I’ve done it in the bathroom at work, trying to be quiet and then come back out like nothing happened. Other times I wait until I get home, but then it’s almost like I can’t relax or think straight until I’ve thrown up. I hate saying that, because it sounds awful, but it’s started feeling like the only way I can calm down after I eat like that.
Do you always feel relieved after making yourself throw up?

Not always… I mean, at first there’s usually this kind of relief, like the panic drops down a little because I did the thing my mind was telling me I had to do. That’s the part that scares me, honestly, because it’s started feeling like the only way I can calm down after I eat.

But it’s not a good relief. It’s not like I feel okay afterward. A lot of times I feel ashamed right away, or tired, or like I can’t believe I did it again. If I’m at work and I’ve gone into the bathroom to make myself throw up, then I have to come back out and act normal, like nothing happened, and that feels awful. And if I’ve waited until I get home, sometimes I’m just rushing straight to the bathroom because I’ve been holding all that panic in, and then afterward I’m relieved but also upset with myself.

So… yes and no. It calms something down in the moment, but then I hate that I needed it to feel calm.
How many times a week do you typically eat a large amount of food in a short period of time?

It’s usually at least a couple times a week… I mean, most weeks. I don’t always write it down or anything, so I’m trying to be honest without giving you some exact number that might not be right, but for months now it’s been happening regularly.

Like, there will be these episodes where I eat way more than I meant to in a short time, and afterward I feel like I have to fix it somehow. A lot of the time that means throwing up, but sometimes I’ll try to make up for it by not eating for a while, or by exercising like I’m trying to burn it off. It kind of depends on where I am and how panicked I feel.

But it’s not just once in a while anymore. Most weeks, there are at least two times where it happens, sometimes more.
How often do you check your weight?

Too often. I mean… I check it a lot, probably more than I should. Sometimes it’s like I tell myself I’m just going to look once, just to know, but then if the number is even a little higher than what I expected, I panic.

It can be the smallest change, and my brain treats it like it means everything is ruined. Like I’ve messed up completely and I’m going to just keep gaining and be fat by the end of the day, even though I know that probably sounds dramatic when I say it out loud. But in the moment it feels real.

And it’s not only the scale. At work, if my waistband feels tight under my apron, I start focusing on it and I can’t stop. I’ll keep thinking about whether I look bigger, whether other people can tell, whether I’ve let myself go. It makes me feel trapped in my own body. So… I don’t know the exact number, but I check my weight and my body a lot because I’m scared of it going up.
Do you consider yourself to be underweight?

I don’t really know how to answer that… like, I don’t think I’m underweight, no. At least not in the way I picture that word meaning. I don’t look at myself and think, “Oh, I’m too thin.” I’m usually thinking the opposite, honestly, or worrying that I’m bigger than I should be.

But I also don’t know what the “official” line is, if you mean by numbers or a chart or something. I just know I don’t feel underweight. If anything, I feel like I’m always trying to keep from going up. So… no, I wouldn’t consider myself underweight, but I don’t know if I’m seeing myself clearly either.
Do you currently have or have you had in the past a period of time where you maintained a significantly low body weight?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t think so, not in a way that someone told me was dangerously low or anything like that. I’ve had times where I was trying really hard to keep my weight down, and I watched the number really closely, but I don’t know if it was ever what you’d call “significantly low.”

I guess part of the problem is I don’t totally trust how I see it. Like, even if someone else might say I looked smaller at a certain time, I don’t know that I would have believed that. I usually just felt like I needed to be careful so it didn’t go up.

So… no, I don’t have a clear period I can point to where I maintained a very low body weight. Not that I know of.
Have you ever had a period where you didn't menstruate for at least three months?

I don’t think so… not that I can clearly remember. My periods have never been something I kept perfect track of, like I know some people mark it on a calendar, but I haven’t really done that consistently. So when you ask “at least three months,” I’m trying to think back and count it out, and I honestly don’t have a definite time where I can say, yes, I went that long without one.

There have been times where I was stressed and it felt like it was late, or I’d be waiting and kind of worrying about it, but I don’t know if it was actually months or just felt long because I was paying attention. I guess if it had been three whole months, I’d probably remember being really scared about it? But I can’t say for sure.

So… I don’t think I’ve had a stretch like that, at least not one I know of.
Have you noticed any changes in your menstrual cycle?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed anything definite. Like I said, I’m not the best at tracking it, so sometimes I’ll think, “Was that later than usual?” but then I don’t know if I’m actually remembering right or just worrying because I’m paying attention to it.

It doesn’t feel like there’s been some obvious big change that I could point to, like a clear pattern I’ve written down or anything. Sometimes stress or just being busy at work makes everything blur together, and then I realize I don’t even know exactly when the last one started. So I can’t really say for sure that my cycle has changed. If it has, I don’t think I’ve noticed it in a reliable way.
Have you ever experienced a time when you didn't have a menstrual period?

I mean… yes, I’ve had times when I didn’t have it right when I expected it, if that’s what you mean. Like, it would be late, or I’d realize, “Wait, I don’t think I got it yet,” and then I’d start trying to remember when the last one was. But I’m not very organized with tracking it, so it’s hard for me to say how long exactly.

I don’t have a clear memory of a really long stretch where I definitely didn’t have a period. It’s more like there have been gaps that felt longer than usual, and then I’d second-guess myself because I couldn’t remember the dates. So… I guess I can’t give you a definite yes in a specific way, like “this happened for this many months.” I just know sometimes it’s been late or I wasn’t sure when it was supposed to come.
Have you ever had a period of time where your menstrual periods stopped?

I don’t really think so… not in a way I can clearly say, “yes, they stopped.” I know I’ve had times where it seemed late, or I suddenly realized I hadn’t noticed it coming when I expected, and then I’d get kind of stuck trying to count backward in my head. But I don’t keep track well enough to say for certain.

Like, if you’re asking whether I went a long stretch with no period at all, I can’t give you a definite yes. I don’t remember a clear time where it just stopped completely. It’s more that there have been times I wasn’t sure when the last one was, or it felt off, but I don’t have dates or anything to prove it. So I guess my honest answer is… I’m not sure, but I don’t think they ever fully stopped for a long time.
Have you ever had a period of at least three consecutive months where you did not have a menstrual period?

I honestly don’t know that I can say yes to three full months. That sounds like something I would probably remember more clearly, but then again I’m really bad at keeping track, so I don’t want to say no like I’m completely certain either.

I’ve had times where it felt late, or where I’d suddenly think, “Wait, when did I last get it?” and I’d try to count back and get confused. But three months in a row with nothing… I don’t have a clear memory of that happening. I don’t have dates written down or anything, so it’s hard for me to be exact, but I don’t think I’ve gone that long without a period.

Sometimes I try to sit with it for a little while, or I tell myself I’m not going to do it this time, but then I get so worked up and panicky that I end up going to the bathroom anyway.

And it’s not just at home, which is part of what scares me. I’ve done it in the bathroom at work, trying to be quiet and then come back out like nothing happened. Other times I wait until I get home, but then it’s almost like I can’t relax or think straight until I’ve thrown up. I hate saying that, because it sounds awful, but it’s started feeling like the only way I can calm down after I eat like that.

doctor.intent: determine if patient's self-induced vomiting is always followed by a sense of relief
doctor.question: Do you always feel relieved after making yourself throw up?

target_item.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
target_item.manifestation: What brings me in is I keep making myself throw up after I eat, sometimes in the bathroom at work or right when I get home, and I hate that it has started feeling like the only way I can calm down.
target_item.reason: The question is directly about how the patient feels after making herself throw up, which is part of the purging behavior described in this symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Not always… I mean, at first there’s usually this kind of relief, like the panic drops down a little because I did the thing my mind was telling me I had to do. That’s the part that scares me, honestly, because it’s started feeling like the only way I can calm down after I eat.

But it’s not a good relief. It’s not like I feel okay afterward. A lot of times I feel ashamed right away, or tired, or like I can’t believe I did it again. If I’m at work and I’ve gone into the bathroom to make myself throw up, then I have to come back out and act normal, like nothing happened, and that feels awful. And if I’ve waited until I get home, sometimes I’m just rushing straight to the bathroom because I’ve been holding all that panic in, and then afterward I’m relieved but also upset with myself.

So… yes and no. It calms something down in the moment, but then I hate that I needed it to feel calm.

doctor.intent: determine frequency of binge eating episodes
doctor.question: How many times a week do you typically eat a large amount of food in a short period of time?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: For months now, most weeks have at least a couple episodes where I eat way more than I meant to and then try to undo it by throwing up, fasting, or exercising it off.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the weekly frequency of episodes involving eating a large amount of food in a short period of time, which is covered by the frequency requirement for binge eating episodes.

patient.answer:
It’s usually at least a couple times a week… I mean, most weeks. I don’t always write it down or anything, so I’m trying to be honest without giving you some exact number that might not be right, but for months now it’s been happening regularly.

Like, there will be these episodes where I eat way more than I meant to in a short time, and afterward I feel like I have to fix it somehow. A lot of the time that means throwing up, but sometimes I’ll try to make up for it by not eating for a while, or by exercising like I’m trying to burn it off. It kind of depends on where I am and how panicked I feel.

But it’s not just once in a while anymore. Most weeks, there are at least two times where it happens, sometimes more.

doctor.intent: Determine the frequency of weight self-monitoring
doctor.question: How often do you check your weight?

target_item.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
target_item.manifestation: If the scale goes up even a little, or my waistband feels tight under my work apron, I panic like I have ruined everything and I will be fat by the end of the day.
target_item.reason: The question is about checking weight, which is most directly related to fear and panic about weight gain, including reactions to the scale going up.

patient.answer:
Too often. I mean… I check it a lot, probably more than I should. Sometimes it’s like I tell myself I’m just going to look once, just to know, but then if the number is even a little higher than what I expected, I panic.

It can be the smallest change, and my brain treats it like it means everything is ruined. Like I’ve messed up completely and I’m going to just keep gaining and be fat by the end of the day, even though I know that probably sounds dramatic when I say it out loud. But in the moment it feels real.

And it’s not only the scale. At work, if my waistband feels tight under my apron, I start focusing on it and I can’t stop. I’ll keep thinking about whether I look bigger, whether other people can tell, whether I’ve let myself go. It makes me feel trapped in my own body. So… I don’t know the exact number, but I check my weight and my body a lot because I’m scared of it going up.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of significantly low weight
doctor.question: Do you consider yourself to be underweight?

target_item.reason: The question asks whether I consider myself underweight, but the symptom profile does not include an item about actual or perceived underweight status.

patient.answer:
I don’t really know how to answer that… like, I don’t think I’m underweight, no. At least not in the way I picture that word meaning. I don’t look at myself and think, “Oh, I’m too thin.” I’m usually thinking the opposite, honestly, or worrying that I’m bigger than I should be.

But I also don’t know what the “official” line is, if you mean by numbers or a chart or something. I just know I don’t feel underweight. If anything, I feel like I’m always trying to keep from going up. So… no, I wouldn’t consider myself underweight, but I don’t know if I’m seeing myself clearly either.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's behavior is more characteristic of bulimia nervosa or anorexia nervosa, binge-eating/purging type

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t think so, not in a way that someone told me was dangerously low or anything like that. I’ve had times where I was trying really hard to keep my weight down, and I watched the number really closely, but I don’t know if it was ever what you’d call “significantly low.”

I guess part of the problem is I don’t totally trust how I see it. Like, even if someone else might say I looked smaller at a certain time, I don’t know that I would have believed that. I usually just felt like I needed to be careful so it didn’t go up.

So… no, I don’t have a clear period I can point to where I maintained a very low body weight. Not that I know of.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's behavior is more aligned with bulimia nervosa or anorexia nervosa, binge-eating/purging type

I don’t think so… not that I can clearly remember. So when you ask “at least three months,” I’m trying to think back and count it out, and I honestly don’t have a definite time where I can say, yes, I went that long without one.

There have been times where I was stressed and it felt like it was late, or I’d be waiting and kind of worrying about it, but I don’t know if it was actually months or just felt long because I was paying attention. I guess if it had been three whole months, I’d probably remember being really scared about it? But I can’t say for sure.

So… I don’t think I’ve had a stretch like that, at least not one I know of.

doctor.intent: Determine if patient's menstrual cycle has been affected

It doesn’t feel like there’s been some obvious big change that I could point to, like a clear pattern I’ve written down or anything.
